Validated result: Authorized dwellings fell from 6,079 in 2021 to 3,538 in 2025 (−41.8%), while population rose from 634,730 to 681,973 (+7.4%).
Interpretation: The near-term supply pipeline moved in the wrong direction. Permits are not completions, so completion tracking is the next essential measurement.

Finding: Household formation and occupied stock were close over the last census decade
Validated result: From 2011 to 2021, private households increased by 41,760 and inhabited dwellings by 42,365.
Interpretation: The decade totals broadly matched, but they do not show location, suitability, tenure, vacancy, or affordability. The post-2021 permit fall remains a warning signal.

Finding: Market housing costs outpaced average gross earnings
Validated result: From 2013 to 2025, average annual gross earnings rose 45.7%, advertised monthly rent rose 50.0%, and existing-apartment prices per m² rose 86.9%.
Interpretation: Monthly advertised rent is the main rent comparison. Advertised rents are asking prices, not signed contracts.

Finding: The raw rent-per-m² history is composition-sensitive
Validated result: Monthly rent divided by rent per m² gives an implied size proxy that falls from 68.7 m² in 2013 to 45.4 m² in 2025.
Interpretation: This ratio uses two averages and is not a measured mean size, but its movement shows that the raw per-m² series should not support a long-run headline. The official methodology also warns that surface and market composition affect advertised-rent statistics.

Finding: Overall purchasing power improved, but that does not resolve housing access
Validated result: CPI-adjusted average gross-earnings purchasing power was 14.9% above its 2013 index level in 2025.
Interpretation: General purchasing power and access to market housing can diverge; CP04 is not used as a market-housing-price measure.

Finding: No clear poverty-housing-cost link was found
Validated result: The income-poverty rate was 14.9% in 2009 and 14.8% in 2025. The change regression has 16 observations, R²=0.07, and p=0.62 for monthly rent growth.
Interpretation: The model has little explanatory power and no statistically clear rent relationship. Household-level linked rent, income, and tenure data are needed.

Finding: Commune rent evidence is selected toward larger places
Validated result: Rents are published for 36 communes with mean 2025 population 13,762, versus 64 suppressed communes averaging 2,915.
Interpretation: The 36-commune rent regression must not be generalized to all 100 communes.
